ssf1918WW1B: Newsreel footage from the Market Street celebration of the end of WWI in San Francisco, 1918.

rv: I think this is really the most boring collection of movies by Archive.org Or maybe just San Francisco is boring. OK, this News Film Footage is interesting, you see really old cars, a celebration on the streets with a big crowd of people and you hear a classic narrator. It's a little bit fun and enough interesting. And it's NOT in color.

The masks are common in local "gatherings". It was too late to protest, and well a party is a party! And other oneliners to follow I am sure. But rhetoric and irony aside, this is a very interesting snippet of history. You could interpret the narrator as setting an anti war tone to the voice over. I don't see any hateful signs that he mentions though. Cool video.
I think it's interesting that the narrator at the end says "They are celebrating that the war is over. And there will never be another." This movie is about WWI.

If you like cats, you'll enjoy this film. Despite being produced in the late 1930's, the quality of the photography and sound is excellent. The footage of the confrontation between the dog and one of the kittens is especially fun to watch.

Everyone loves cat videos, so no doubt kids in the 1930s ate this up. The kittens are cute. The film glosses over that farmers drowned cats so they wouldn't be overrun with them. Today, it's unthinkable to suburban people because cats are considered pets. What was "mother cat" called before it was a mother? Dialogue and sound effects (cat and dog noises) are looped.
